title: canary rollout personal scratchpad - avery hudson
content:
Quick scratchpad for upcoming canary rollout (hosted API):

Context: deploying model-serving changes + routing fallback improvements (PR #842). Aim: canary -> progressive ramp to 20% over 72h, then evaluate for stable rollout. Notes to self / checklist for release day.

Goals:
- Validate no regression in gen latency or error rate vs baseline (v1.2.3)
- Keep p95 latency <= baseline + 20%
- Token cost delta tracked (Optimize metrics)
- No customer-impacting errors > 1% HTTP 5xx or model-timeouts

High-level plan (rough):
1) Prep (T-72h)
   - Confirm pinned model artifacts: model-serving:v2026-02-20-rc (artifact hash d4f3a2) — avoid auto-upgrades
   - Create canary route: /v1/generate?route=canary-avery (routing rule + header X-Canary:true)
   - Deploy canary pods to us-west2, dedicated node-pool (small batch: 4 pods)
   - Feature flag: rollout.canary.avery = true (ff service)
   - Add synthetic traffic jobs (loadgen) -> 10 rps baseline, variable seq len 128/256
   - Postman collection for manual smoke tests (docs link in Confluence)

2) Day 0 (launch)
   - 0 -> 1% traffic (3h soak) -> 5% (12h) -> 10% (24h) -> 20% (72h total)
   - Manual checks at each step (see checklist below)
   - Notify #canary-notifications Slack channel before each ramp (Jamie to post)
   - Safety guard: automated rollback if any of rollback triggers fire (see below)

Rollback / safety triggers (automated + manual):
- HTTP 5xx rate > 1% for > 5m
- Error ratio on model responses (decoder failures) > 0.5% for > 5m
- p95 latency increase > 2x baseline for > 5m OR p95 increases > baseline + 200ms consistently
- GPU memory thrashing / OOMs on more than 2 pods in 30m
- Key customer 1:1 alert (Pager duty) -> immediate halt

Monitoring / Dashboards to watch:
- Dash: /dashboards/canary/summary (p50/p95, 5xx rate, token cost delta)
- Logs: ELK filter: route:canary-avery AND level:ERROR
- Traces: Jaeger trace sample rate 100% for canary routes for first 24h
- Infra: GCE/GKE node metrics (gpu_util, cpu_iowait), network errors
- Cache metrics: KV cache hit ratio (affects latency for long-chat workloads)

Smoke tests (manual):
- simple-gen: prompt "Summarize infra plan" -> expect coherent summary, no hallucination hazards
- stream test: ensure chunked responses stream correctly (no truncated streams)
- function-calling path: simulate tools calls (mock tool) 50 samples
- embedding path: sanity-check against baseline embeddings (cosine similarity > 0.98 for short inputs)

Checklist (to tick on release):
- [ ] Confirm artifact hash and pin in deployment config (no auto-rolls)
- [ ] Create canary route + route config in console
- [ ] Update routing policy: percentage buckets + fallback to stable if incompatible
- [ ] Start synth traffic jobs and validate baseline metrics
- [ ] Create Slack notification thread and post pre-launch note
- [ ] Enable extended tracing for canary (24h)
- [ ] Monitor heap/GPU memory during first 3 ramps
- [ ] Check token billing anomalies in cost dashboard (unexpected spike?)

Version pinning notes (important):
- Must pin both model artifact and runtime image. If only model is pinned, runtime auto-upgrade can change kernel selection and cause perf regressions.
- Example: pin to model-serving:v2026-02-20-rc + runtime:inference-runtime:2.6.1
- For dedicated customers, confirm per-customer overrides (some have pinned earlier versions) — check customer-configs table (db: customer_overrides)

Open questions / TODOs:
- QA: Should we run subset of long-context tests (seq=2048) during canary? Pros: catch regressions; Cons: may skew latency metrics. Proposal: run separate long-context synth jobs (do not route real traffic).
- Automated rollback: who can unsuspend it? Currently ops lead + release owner (me). Need to confirm 2nd approver in case I'm OOO. @Priya?
- Post-rollout eval: schedule prompt-set quality eval (compare top-5 prompts from customer telemetry) — link to eval harness PR RINF-3421.

Backout plan (if need full revert):
- Step 1: set rollout.canary.avery = false (stop routing new traffic)
- Step 2: scale down canary pods to 0 and scale up stable pods
- Step 3: verify stable route p95/p50 within baseline within 30m
- Step 4: run targeted smoke tests and close incident

Notes from last dry-run (2026-02-12):
- Observed small p95 spike (~12%) at 5% traffic during large-token requests (>512). Root cause: cache cold-start + kernel fallback. Mitigation: pre-warm KV cache (run warmup script across canary pods) and increase batch timeout default from 5ms -> 8ms.
- Actioned: warmup script added to canary deploy job (PR#836). Need to verify warmup runs on new pods.

Log snippets to watch for (examples):
- "kv_cache_miss_remote_fetch" spikes -> indicates cache misses causing backend fetches
- "decoder_timeout" -> repeated patterns before a model OOM

Communication plan:
- Pre-launch: slack post + short ops-email to pd@redwood.ai (Jamie)
- Mid-rollout: hourly updates for first 12h, then every 6h
- Post-rollout: summary + metrics + any regressions in Confluence page linked above

Final reminders:
- Tag PR with "canary-avery" and link to release ticket (RINF-3421)
- Ensure synthetic traffic job has tag owner=avery for easier filtering
- If rollback happens, collect full traces and open follow-up incident ticket with IA (incident-assigned)

-- end of scratchpad --

(Loose notes / thoughts: keep prompts representative of customer mix, prioritize low-latency interactive flows in first 24h. If any uncertainty, default to halting ramp and investigating rather than pushing forward.)
